2026-12-02.title: First Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Jesus is sent by the Father
2026-12-02.verse: And the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.
theo: Paul thanks God for the gifts given to the Corinthians as they “wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ,” and assures them: “God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son.” The whole Annunciation season rests on God's faithfulness.

Jesus speaks of the One who sent him: “The one who sent me is true… he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.” The Son's mission flows from the Father's love and is lived in constant obedience. Christmas is the arrival of the One sent; our joy is to be sent in turn.
outline: Ask: who has been faithful to you through everything?
He will strengthen you to the end.
Jesus comes from the Father and speaks the Father's words.
The Son always does what pleases the Father.
live: Recall one way God was faithful to you this year and thank him.
Before each decision today ask: does this please the Father?
2026-12-02.prayer: Faithful God, you called me into fellowship with your Son. As he always did what pleased you, let me do your will, knowing you never leave me alone. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana Christ unites us to his own communion with the Father. Receiving him, we are drawn into that life where no one is alone.

quick: Jesus is the One sent by the Father.
We are never alone when we do the Father's will.
2026-12-02.action: Thank God for one sign of his faithfulness this year.
2026-12-02.question: Do my choices please the Father?

family.explain: Jesus said: my Father is always with me, because I do what pleases him. God is with us too, especially when we do good.
family.intention: We pray for lonely people: grandparents, migrants and the sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Who do we know who is lonely, and how can we show them they are not alone?”

pm.open: Faithful Father, you never leave your children alone. Gather us in your Son's name, speak to us through your word, and make us faithful as you are faithful. Amen.
share: Paul says: God is faithful (1 Corinthians 1:9). When have I experienced God's faithfulness?
Jesus says: I always do what is pleasing to him (John 8:29). What would please the Father in my life this week?
Who around me feels alone, and what can I do for them?
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's faithfulness to every generation.
For those who feel abandoned, that they may experience the Father's presence.
For migrants and families separated by distance, that love may bridge the miles.
For the sick in hospitals and at home, that they may be comforted.
For our prayer group, that we may grow in fidelity to God's will.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you lived in constant communion with the Father. Keep us united to you, make us faithful in small things, and let no one around us feel alone. Amen.

illus: An elderly widow in Kottayam, whose children were all abroad, said: “Every evening at six I sit before the picture of the Sacred Heart and tell him about my day. I am never alone.” Faith had turned her loneliness into communion.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul begins his first letter to the Corinthians with thanksgiving. Their community had many problems: divisions, scandals, confusion. Yet Paul first thanks God for the gifts they had received, and assures them: God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son (1 Corinthians 1:9).

The whole season of Annunciation rests on this one truth: God is faithful. He promised a Saviour to Abraham, to David, to the prophets; and he kept his word. When we feel unfaithful, weak and divided, God remains faithful. His faithfulness is not based on our goodness but on his own heart.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of his relationship with the Father: the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him (John 8:29). These words reveal the secret of Jesus' life: constant communion with the Father.

Many people today are lonely. Old parents whose children are abroad; young people far from home in cities and hostels; migrants in the Gulf; the sick in hospitals. Jesus tells us that, united with him, we too are never alone. The Father who was with the Son is with those who belong to the Son.

But notice the second half of Jesus' sentence: for I always do what is pleasing to him. Communion with God grows through obedience. When we do the Father's will in small things, we discover that he is near.
This Nombu, let us practise a simple examination each night: what did I do today that pleased the Father? What did I do that did not? Then a short act of thanks and a short act of sorrow.
And let us visit someone who is lonely this week, in person or by phone. Through us, God can say to them what Jesus said: you are not alone. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: my Father is always with me. God is always with you too, even when you feel alone!

intro: Theme: “The faithful God and the One he sends.”
God is faithful; Jesus, sent by the Father, always does what pleases him.

sub: He calls us into fellowship with his Son.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
I have much to say about you and much to condemn; but the one who sent me is true, and I declare to the world what I have heard from him.
points.apply: Thank God for his faithfulness this year.

sub: When the Son of Man is lifted up, we will know “I am he”.
The Cross reveals who Jesus is.
q: You are my witnesses, says the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.
So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.”
points.apply: Spend a moment before the crucifix today.

sub: The Father is always with the Son.
Doing his will, we are never alone.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you.
And the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.
points.apply: Before each decision ask: does this please the Father?

concl: God is faithful to his promises.
The One sent is coming; we are never alone.
2026-12-02.resolve: Pray each morning: “Father, today I want to please you.”
